description: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria porri characterized by purple-centered lesions on onion foliage and seed stalks.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked lesions that turn brown to purplish with yellow halos.
Lesions enlarge and girdle leaves causing them to collapse and dry up.
Dark brown powdery fungal spores visible on leaf surfaces during humid mornings.
generalInformation: Favored by warm temperatures (21–30°C) and prolonged leaf wetness or relative humidity above 80%.
prevention: Maintain well-drained soil and avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
Ensure proper crop spacing to promote foliage aeration and rapid drying.
Apply protective copper or mancozeb-based fungicides during humid weather spells.
Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-allium crops.

description: Destructive disease caused by Peronospora destructor that causes leaf dieback and stunted bulb development.
symptoms: Pale green to yellowish oval patches on older foliage.
Fine violet-gray velvety fungal growth on infected leaf areas under damp conditions.
Infected leaves collapse, turn brown, and dry from the tips downward.
generalInformation: Overwinters in infected onion bulbs and spreads quickly in cool (10–18°C), misty or humid climates.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free onion sets and certified seeds.
Avoid planting in sheltered or poorly drained fields with restricted air flow.
Destroy and plow under crop residues immediately after harvest.

description: Vibrant, upright tubular green foliage indicating robust bulb formation and nutrient balance.
symptoms: Smooth, deep blue-green hollow leaf blades without blemishes.
Firm sheath attachment and clean neck tissue.
Strong erect growth habit.
generalInformation: Optimal photosynthetic leaf area is essential for maximum bulb expansion and storage longevity.
prevention: Provide consistent moisture through drip lines and balanced sulfur-potassium fertilization.
Conduct regular scouting for thrips and early leaf lesions.

description: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris, considered one of the most damaging brassica diseases worldwide.
symptoms: V-shaped yellow chlorotic lesions starting at leaf margins with base pointing toward midrib.
Leaf veins within chlorotic lesions turn distinctly black or dark brown.
Severe systemic infection causes premature leaf drop and curd discoloration.
generalInformation: Bacterial pathogen enters leaves through hydathodes (marginal pores) and stomata during warm, humid rains.
prevention: Use hot-water treated or certified disease-free seed.
Rotate out of brassicas/crucifers for at least 3 years.
Avoid handling or cultivating plants when foliage is wet.

description: Fungal-like oomycete infection caused by Hyaloperonospora parasitica affecting leaves and young curds.
symptoms: Yellowish, angular chlorotic spots on the upper leaf surface.
Fluffy white to light gray fungal growth on the underside of leaves.
Curd surfaces may develop grayish-black internal vascular discoloration.
generalInformation: Common in cool, damp seedbeds and overcast seasons; thrives in fog and heavy morning dew.
prevention: Promote air movement by thinning seedlings and optimizing field spacing.
Water crops early in the morning so leaves dry quickly in the sun.
Apply preventive bio-fungicides during prolonged cool, foggy conditions.

description: Robust, waxy blue-green brassica foliage supporting tight, healthy curd formation.
symptoms: Broad, thick leaves with a healthy whitish bloom (cuticle wax).
No marginal yellowing or blackened vein architecture.
Vigorous central growth and clean petioles.
generalInformation: Well-nourished cauliflower canopies shield developing heads from solar scorch.
prevention: Maintain adequate soil boron and molybdenum levels alongside balanced NPK nutrition.
Ensure regular moisture retention with organic mulch.

description: Quarantine fungal pathogen caused by Puccinia horiana that damages decorative floriculture crops.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots (dimples) up to 5mm wide on upper leaf surfaces.
Raised, waxy buff-to-white colored pustules (telia) on leaf undersides.
Leaves become necrotic, curl downward, and dry up completely in severe outbreaks.
generalInformation: Spread by windborne basidiospores; requires 100% relative humidity and free moisture for spore germination.
prevention: Purchase only certified disease-free stock cuttings.
Isolate new incoming plants in a quarantine area for 2–3 weeks.
Reduce greenhouse humidity below 75% with ventilation and bottom heat.

description: Fungal leaf spot caused by Septoria chrysanthemella resulting in progressive lower-leaf necrosis.
symptoms: Circular dark brown to black spots with distinct margins on lower leaves.
Spots may coalesce into large dead necrotic patches.
Infected leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely, moving from base upwards.
generalInformation: Fungal spores are splashed upward from soil and fallen leaf debris by rain or overhead watering.
prevention: Strip and dispose of infected bottom leaves promptly.
Use drip irrigation to keep blossom and foliage dry.
Apply protective copper or chlorothalonil fungicides at the first sign of spotting.

description: Lush, deeply lobed aromatic foliage with vibrant chlorophyll pigmentation.
symptoms: Rich deep-green serrated leaves with supple texture.
Undersides completely free of raised pustules or fungal mycelium.
Strong lateral branching and healthy apical buds.
generalInformation: Healthy chrysanthemum foliage provides the essential photosynthetic base for radiant floral blooms.
prevention: Provide high light intensity and balanced feeding with iron and magnesium.
Maintain consistent airflow around dense floral canopies.

description: Pervasive fungal infection caused by Podosphaera xanthii covering cucurbit foliage in a talcum-powder like coating.
symptoms: White powdery circular spots on both leaf surfaces, petioles, and stems.
Spots expand rapidly to cover whole leaf blades with white talc-like spores.
Leaves turn chlorotic, senesce early, and leave fruit vulnerable to sunscald.
generalInformation: Favored by high humidity, low light, and warm dry temperatures without requiring free liquid water.
prevention: Select resistant or tolerant cucumber hybrid varieties.
Apply potassium bicarbonate, sulfur, or neem oil solutions at first notice.
Prune dense vine growth to improve sunlight penetration and air movement.

description: Rapidly destructive water mold caused by Pseudoperonospora cubensis causing scorched foliage appearance.
symptoms: Angular, bright yellow spots bounded strictly by leaf veins on the upper surface.
Dark grayish-purple downy mold growth visible on the underside of corresponding spots.
Infected areas turn brown and necrotic quickly, creating a 'burned' canopy look.
generalInformation: Known as 'cucurbit wildfire' due to how quickly it can destroy an entire field within days of wet weather.
prevention: Plant early in the season or choose downy-mildew resistant cultivars.
Never use overhead irrigation; ensure leaves stay dry through the evening.
Apply preventive systemic fungicides ahead of wet forecasts.

description: Expansive, vibrant green palmate cucurbit leaves with strong vine vigor.
symptoms: Large, uniformly green lobed leaves with crisp serrated margins.
Clean leaf surfaces free of powder or angular yellowing.
Active tendril development and continuous flower setting.
generalInformation: Vigorous vine canopy maintains optimum carbohydrate production for crisp fruit development.
prevention: Trellis vines vertically for maximum air circulation and easy monitoring.
Maintain steady soil moisture to prevent water stress.

description: A common fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani affecting leaves, stems, and fruits of tomatoes.
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings (target-like pattern) on older leaves.
Yellow halos surrounding leaf lesions.
Premature leaf drop leading to sunscald on fruits.
generalInformation: Thrives in warm, humid weather and spreads via rain splashes and wind.
prevention: Ensure proper plant spacing for good air circulation.
Water at the base of the plant using drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.
Apply copper-based or bio-fungicide sprays upon early detection.
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.

description: A devastating water mold infection caused by Phytophthora infestans that can quickly destroy entire tomato crops.
symptoms: Large, irregularly shaped water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems.
White fungal fuzzy growth on leaf undersides in high humidity.
Rapidly turning dark brown and collapsing plant tissue.
generalInformation: The same pathogen that caused the Irish Potato Famine; spreads rapidly during cool, wet conditions.
prevention: Destroy and discard infected plant debris immediately (do not compost).
Avoid overhead watering and minimize leaf wetness duration.
Select certified disease-free transplants and blight-resistant cultivars.

description: Vibrant, healthy tomato foliage with optimal chlorophyll levels and no visible pathogen damage.
symptoms: Deep green uniform leaf coloration.
Firm, upright leaf stems without spots or discoloration.
Even leaf margins and active healthy growth.
generalInformation: Healthy tomato foliage supports strong photosynthetic activity for high fruit yield.
prevention: Maintain consistent soil moisture and balanced N-P-K fertilization.
Scout foliage weekly for early signs of pests or disease.
